newsitem.title: UK: London details rules for order-driven share trade.
newsitem.headline: London details rules for order-driven share trade.

text.p: The London Stock Exchange (LSE) on Monday detailed its rules for a new automated order book for the top 100 FTSE stocks due to be launched later this year.
The plans include a timetable of milestones which must be achieved by mid-July in order to confirm a planned starting date of October 20.

In a statement the LSE said that after the latest review of plans with the market it had decided to amend the pre-opening time for order inputting to 0800 a.m. (local), and opening would be at 0830 a.m.. Deletion of orders is to be allowed for 30 minutes after the close, it added.

A feature of the order-driven system that allows execution to be suspended will now only be cut in response to a 10 percent price movement (previously seen at 5.0 percent), and for no more than 10 minutes (previously planned for 15 minutes).
A sliding scale of tick sizes is to be introduced so that lower priced shares can be traded in proportionally similar increments to higher-priced ones, the LSE said.
This means that shares priced up to 5.00 stg will have ticks of 0.25p, 5.00 to 10.00 stg shares will have 0.5p ticks and over 10.00 stg the increment will be one penny.
Over the next two months the exchange said it planned to roll out a programme of nationwide training seminars and would also develop courses for new skills linked to the system.
